title: When One Child Hits Another | Parenting Rewind
description:
One child hits and both children look to you for what happens next. A practical pause-and-rewind response for parents.

General parenting education; every child and family is different.
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: One child hits and both children look to you for what happens next. Demanding an instant apology before anyone is calm can produce words without safety or learning. Before reacting, pause for one breath so the next words can be short, clear, and useful. Block the hit, separate if needed, and say: I will not let you hit; hands stay safe; we will talk when bodies are calmer. Safety comes first, followed by a clear rule, a related response, and repair when the child can participate.

source.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source.title: Tips for Creating Rules

claim_limits: The suggested wording is an example, not a guarantee.
Families should adapt expectations to age, development, safety and individual needs.
